groups.summary:
**The group's framing repeats the potts error at directory scale: "OED" is a shared word hiding two different design spaces.** proteinsmc's `oed/` optimizes *SMC sampler hyperparameters* (`OEDDesign`: population_size, n_generations, diversification_ratio → `OEDPredictedVariables`: information_gain, barrier-crossing, JSD, geometric fitness). asr's `oed/` optimizes *ancestral-reconstruction experiment design* (`ASRDesign`: n_leaves, branch_length, lambda_val, mutation_rate_noise_std → `ASRPredictedVariables`: accuracy_overall/accuracy_root, consensus_bias, epistatic error). The two struct pairs share **zero** predicted-variable fields and only 3 of 8+ design fields. Every "asr already has this file; merge" claim in the block rests on filename identity, not lineage.

Verdicts: C1 CONFIRMED (asr's gp.py is genuinely the advanced fork). C8 NEEDS_QUALIFICATION (smc_tree is *importable and imported at runtime today* — I ran it; it is the plan's own phase-3 gate, already satisfied). C2, C6, C9, C10 REFUTED. C3, C4, C5, C7, C11 NEEDS_QUALIFICATION.

Three findings the plan must not ship without:
1. **`oed/opt.py` is not a "real payload" — it is mathematically broken.** `opt.py:63` builds `fim[i,j] = d_info_i * d_info_j`, the outer product of finite-difference derivatives of a **single scalar** (`information_gain`). That is rank-1 by construction, so `jnp.linalg.det(fim)` at `opt.py:68` is identically 0 for every design. `run.py:153-157` then takes `argmax` over an array of float noise. The BO acquisition selects designs at random. Moving it to asr ports a silent no-op into a repo whose own acquisition (`asr/oed/gp.py:276 score_candidates_batch`, masked uncertainty sampling) actually works.
2. **`oed/experiment.py` → asr is destructive as written.** "asr already has this file; merge" — asr's `oed/experiment.py` is a live 308-line trex ancestral-reconstruction pipeline with bucketed static-shape padding, imported by 3 scripts + `tests/test_oed_integration.py`. proteinsmc's is a 179-line SMC-run-and-read-ArrayRecord metrics harness. They share a filename and nothing else. Any "merge" that treats them as versions of one file loses asr's working pipeline.
3. **The metrics split's "only consumer" premise is false in both halves.** `rg` across all eight repos: the analysis half's *only* consumer anywhere is `proteinsmc/oed/experiment.py` itself. asr consumes **none** of it (asr's `shannon_entropy` at `scripts/visualize_antigenic_uncertainty.py:20` is `scipy.stats.entropy` aliased — another shared-word collision; asr's real one is `asr/metrics.py:10 sequence_entropy`). And the "SMC-intrinsic half (…, ESS)" names a function that does not exist in `metrics.py` — ESS is computed inline at `sampling/particle_systems/smc.py:151`. The two named SMC-intrinsic functions have **zero** call sites in `src/` outside their own re-export.

Also: proteinsmc is uninstallable standalone today (`uv run` fails: "prxteinmpnn was not found in the package registry"), so every runtime check in this group had to be run inside asr's venv against `asr/vendor/proteinsmc/src` — which `diff -rq` confirms is byte-identical to the source repo's `oed/` right now.

Three findings deserve the parent agent's attention because they repeat the potts failure mode:

1. **D12 is the same error shape as potts.** The plan read the top-level `if sampler_type_upper in {...}` chain and concluded "a single dispatch on a string — exactly the switch the KERNELS registry removes." Reading the file shows the string chain is 30 of 393 lines. groups.assessment:
Mixed. The verifier applied the potts test genuinely and well on the SOURCE side — D12 in particular is a real catch of the exact failure mode (top-level dispatch shape read as the whole file), and I re-confirmed its structure independently (`initialization_factory.py` is 393 lines; the blackjax `match` is at `:198-249`, the PRSMC island constructor at `:293-393` — the verifier's line cites are off by a few but the architecture claim is exact). D2/D3/D4/D8/D9/D13 hold under re-search. It correctly ran the runtime-vs-type-import distinction in BOTH directions, including the unusual reverse case at D4 (`config_unpacker.py:12` is a module-level runtime import into `models/`, making it a live edge even though nothing imports the file).

But the verifier reproduced the potts error itself on the DESTINATION side, three times, and in one case shipped that error as its headline finding.

The pattern: it read the source file in full every time, and read the destination only as far as the name the plan gave it. D1 — it verified `xtrax/tiling/bucket.py` "genuinely owns the replacement" without noticing that module's own docstring says padding must run "on the host, **before** the JIT boundary... Pads with NumPy", while proteinsmc's `padding.py` is device-side `jnp` intended to run inside jit; and `rg 'masked_mean|masked_sum'` over `xtrax/src` returns zero, so a third of the file has no destination at all. D5 — the entire destination check is the sentence "verified to exist: `xtrax/src/xtrax/distributed/sharding.py` is present"; an `ls`. `rg 'pmap' ~/projects/xtrax/src` returns **zero hits**, so the named destination cannot host a `jax.pmap` helper. D6/D10 — it asserted the capability gap ("xtrax's design deliberately does not benchmark", "Neither measures elapsed time") from the shape of the one API the plan named, without searching the destination repo; `xtrax/loop/compile_time_clock.py:100-110` is `time.perf_counter()` + `jax.block_until_ready()` around a jitted call, the same idiom as `benchmark_batch_size`.

The most serious problem is D14, because it is the verifier's own affirmative discovery rather than an inherited one, it is flagged to the parent as one of three findings deserving attention, and it is false. It reads `[tool.setuptools.packages.find]` and glosses it "i.e. `find_packages()`, which discovers only directories containing `__init__.py`; the namespace variant would be `find-namespace`" — reasoning from the setup.py API name to pyproject behavior. In pyproject.toml the `namespaces` option **defaults to True** (`setuptools/config/expand.py: def find_packages(*, namespaces=True, ...)`), so the finder is already `PEP420PackageFinder`. Empirically, a minimal project with that exact stanza and a subdirectory carrying no `__init__.py` discovers `['pkg', 'pkg.sub']` on setuptools 68/75/84. There is no install-time break, and the prescribed remedy (`[tool.setuptools.packages.find-namespace]`) is not a key setuptools accepts — `find-namespace` does not appear in its validation schema.

Second problem, and the one the task singles out as most dangerous: a CONFIRMED delete whose exhaustive-search claim is false. D1's evidence reads "Symbol sweep for `SEQ_BUCKETS|...|masked_mean|masked_sum` → every hit is inside `proteinsmc/src/proteinsmc/padding.py:7-134` itself." Running that sweep over proteinsmc + asr returns six hits outside it. The verifier ran the shared-word test on prolix's `padding.py` and correctly separated it, then missed the two modules that are actually the same lineage — `asr/src/asr/oed/padding.py` and `aminx/src/aminx/tiling/buckets.py`, which share the opening docstring pattern, the byte-identical `raise ValueError(f"... exceeds all buckets {BUCKETS}")`, and a byte-identical `masked_mean` signature and body. Its regexes (`from \.\.?padding`, `import padding`) structurally cannot match `from asr.oed.padding import (`. The delete itself survives — nothing imports proteinsmc's copy — so I am qualifying rather than overturning; but the stated basis for the CONFIRMED is not what was actually run, and the plan's dedup rationale collapses once the live copies are visible.

I did not re-check D7 and D11 in depth; both verdicts are internally consistent with source I did read and neither turns on a destination claim.

groups.summary:
Seven claims audited by reading both sides in full; ten verdicts returned (X1, X2, X3, X6 each split where the plan makes two separable assertions). **Three REFUTED, three NEEDS_QUALIFICATION, four CONFIRMED.** The plan's R5 self-catch was real but is the smallest of the problems in this group.

**The dominant failure pattern here is not name-matching on modules — it is name-matching on FUNCTION SIGNATURES.** Four of the six adverse verdicts come from assuming that because two functions take a `batch_size`, or produce a "ladder", or live under a module called "sharding", they compute the same thing. In every case reading the body showed a different return kind, a different axis, or a different unit.

**REFUTED — X1a (`chunked_map` -> `safe_map`).** The plan lists one caveat (divisibility); there are four differences, and two break immediately. `chunked_map` UNPACKS a tuple payload into positional args (`jax_utils.py:55-58`); `safe_map` passes it as one arg. `mutation.py:217-221` and `runner.py:126-131` both pass tuples to two-arg callables — a mechanical swap yields a wrong-arity TypeError. `safe_map` also has no `static_args` (both `smc_tree.py` sites use it), raises IndexError on empty pytrees, and silently escalates to full `jax.vmap` when `n <= batch_size` — materializing the whole population, which is the memory blow-up the chunking existed to prevent.

**REFUTED — X3b (`memory.py` -> `MemoryBudget`).** Wrong output kind. `auto_tune_batch_size` *selects* a batch size by wall-clock benchmarking the real fitness fn and feeds the scalar back into `get_fitness_function(batch_size=...)` (`runner.py:131,139-144`). `MemoryBudget`+`BatchPlanner` never selects a batch size — `AxisDecision.batch_size` is documented "from spec" (`plan.py:96-106`); it takes the batch size as given and chooses a *strategy* to fit a byte budget. Latency optimizer vs memory demoter. Also `models/memory.py` is not dead: five live consumers including a runtime call path.

**REFUTED — X5 (annealing absorbs prolix's ladder).** The clearest potts-test hit in the group, and the highest-risk one. `ANNEALING_REGISTRY` is indexed by TIME (scalar beta per `current_step`); `generate_temperature_ladder` is indexed by REPLICA (a `(n_replicas,)` vector held simultaneously in parallel tempering, `replica_exchange.py:284`). Orthogonal axes, different arity, incompatible signature — and critically, **inverted units**: proteinsmc anneals beta ascending, prolix builds temperature in Kelvin ascending (300K→400K in its own test, `test_replica_exchange.py:12`). Since β = 1/k_BT, registering it as-is anneals the wrong direction with no type error — exactly the temperature-inversion class BATHOS.md was written after.

**NEEDS_QUALIFICATION — X2, X4, X7.** X2: the DELETE is sound (`distribute` is genuinely dead across all repos), but `xtrax.distributed.sharding` has no data-parallel primitive at all — `ShardingPolicy.apply_to_pytree` returns a tree of `PartitionSpec` *objects* and never moves an array. X4 (destructive): deadness survives a full eight-repo search, but only 1 of 6 functions maps to xtrax — `bucketize` pads the LEADING axis host-side with NumPy and raises on overflow, while `pad_sequence` pads the TRAILING axis in `jnp` and `pad_population` silently truncates; the four masking helpers have no counterpart. Also asr already forked this file live (`asr/oed/padding.py`, imported at `experiment.py:19`) with N/K/q ladders. X7: `xtrax.tiling` passes its own potts test — two unrelated domains drive it, and the `xtrax.inference` coupling was deliberately severed (`roles.py:1-8`) — but generality holds only for leading-axis, statically-known cardinality.

**CONFIRMED — X1b, X2b, X3a, X6.** X1b is confirmed *and understated*: R5's "can start failing" should read "fails on the library defaults" — `pop_size=100`, `inference_batch_size=64`, 100 % 64 = 36, and the two `chunked_map` sites map over the population axis. The plan also audits the wrong axis, checking 64 against `pop_size` when the pre-existing `safe_map` at `smc_tree.py:290` applies the same 64 to `num_leaves`.

**One new finding the plan does not account for (X6b, REFUTED):** §4's "`import proteinsmc` pulls in jax + xtrax and nothing else" is false. xtrax's runtime deps are `grain`, `orbax-checkpoint`, `optax`, `equinox`, `numpy` and `pytest-asyncio` (a test package in the runtime list), and it hard-pins `jax>=0.10.2,<0.11` against proteinsmc's bare unpinned `jax`. Q5 should cost the pin as three things, not two: alpha cadence, the 3.13 floor, and a single-minor jax ceiling inherited by everything downstream in the §2 DAG.

**Cross-cutting hazard worth surfacing to the plan author:** xtrax's planner *knows* about the divisibility trap and ships it as policy — `plan.py:131-132` Rule 5 emits `SafeMap` with a warning under a documented "deferred-failure contract", so for proteinsmc's own defaults `BatchPlanner` returns a plan whose execution then raises in `safe_map`. Phase 4's verification step ("`xtrax plan` reproduces the batch sizes the deleted heuristics chose") will pass while producing a plan that crashes at runtime.

Key paths: `/home/marielle/projects/proteinsmc/src/proteinsmc/utils/jax_utils.py`, `/home/marielle/projects/proteinsmc/src/proteinsmc/utils/memory.py`, `/home/marielle/projects/proteinsmc/src/proteinsmc/padding.py`, `/home/marielle/projects/proteinsmc/src/proteinsmc/utils/annealing.py`, `/home/marielle/projects/xtrax/src/xtrax/transforms/map.py`, `/home/marielle/projects/xtrax/src/xtrax/tiling/plan.py`, `/home/marielle/projects/xtrax/src/xtrax/tiling/bucket.py`, `/home/marielle/projects/prolix/src/prolix/pt/temperature.py`.

It read both implementations end-to-end on every claim I spot-checked, and its three REFUTED verdicts are the real substance of the audit. I independently re-derived and upheld the two most consequential ones. X1a: I read jax_utils.py:47-60 and xtrax/transforms/map.py:8-40 in full and confirmed the inverted tuple convention (`func(*x, **kwargs)` vs `jax.vmap(fn)(xs)`), the missing `static_args`, the missing empty-leaf guard, and the vmap escalation; the breaking call sites are real (mutation.py's `fn(k, seq)` is genuinely two-arg, runner.py:126-131 genuinely builds a `(key, array)` tuple). X5: I read prolix/pt/temperature.py in full — 'Minimum temperature in Kelvin', returns `(n_replicas,)`, unjitted, no `current_step` — the beta-vs-Kelvin inversion finding is correct and is the sharpest catch in the group. X4, the one destructive claim, I re-searched independently across all eight repos (`rg 'proteinsmc.padding|proteinsmc import padding'` plus a `find` for every `*padding*` file): zero importers, the only hit being a `SOURCES.txt` manifest line in vendored egg-info. The verifier's deadness proof holds, and its refusal to justify the delete as 'xtrax owns this' was the right call.

Where it slipped, it slipped in exactly one direction: it applied the potts test rigorously to every move OUT of proteinsmc, and stopped applying it when the claim was about xtrax's own quality. X3a is the clear instance — it confirmed a uniqueness claim ('the only implementation with compiler-derived memory budgeting') from two files with no search reported, when a two-minute `rg` shows the allocator half implemented five times and the compiler half three times, and when the plan's own §7 table says 'Memory-budget estimation (4 implementations)' twelve pages after §6.2 says 'the only implementation'. Worse, it praised xtrax for failing loud against proteinsmc's silent fallback, having read only the two opt-in helper functions; the planner path a proteinsmc adapter would actually go through (plan.py:442-455) has two nested bare `except Exception` blocks and a hardcoded 4 GiB default — a wider silent swallow than the incumbent it is meant to replace.

X7 is the one place a literal name-match slipped through. The verifier's own methodology note says it checked 'runtime instantiations by independent domains,' but the check it ran was `rg 'AxisSpec\('` — and three of the hits it cited as prolix driving xtrax are constructions of prolix's OWN AxisSpec class, which carries an `axis_index` field xtrax's does not have. Same word, different class, and the two consumers it cited as proof of generality are better read as proof that neither could adopt the layer unmediated. That said: the verifier caught the deeper structural issue in the same claim anyway (the deferred-failure contract at plan.py:131-132, where `BatchPlanner` emits a plan it knows `safe_map` will raise on), which is the finding that actually matters for phase 4's verification gate. Net: strong work, one blind spot pointed at the destination repo rather than the source.

groups.summary:
Six claims verified against source on both sides. Two clean CONFIRMs (P1a, P6), one REFUTED (P1b), four NEEDS_QUALIFICATION.

THE POTTS-SHAPED ERROR IN THIS GROUP IS P1b. `PROTEINMPNN_X_INT = 21` (proteinsmc/utils/constants.py:115) is named after ProteinMPNN, but `AA_CHAR_TO_INT_MAP = restype_order` (:113) is the AlphaFold/ColabDesign ordering — translation.py:60's own docstring says "ColabDesign's scheme". And 21 matches NEITHER convention: X is index 20 in the real MPNN alphabet (proxide/io/parsing/mappings.py:23, aminx/utils/aa_convert.py:16, aminx/potts/model.py:40) and 20 in proxide's AF-with-X (`unk_restype_index`, residues.py:646). The plan routes this constant to DELETE alongside `restypes`/`AA_CHAR_TO_INT_MAP` on the grounds that "the core needs only q: int" — but it is the stop/unknown sentinel of the codon path the plan explicitly KEEPS, read at translation.py:73,95, mutation.py:76, cai.py:65 and used as the fill value of `CODON_INT_TO_RES_INT_JAX` (constants.py:120-124). §4 splits a live dependency down the middle. It also has a live consequence today: `PROTEINMPNN_TO_ESM_AA_MAP_JAX` is sized 20 (constants.py:272-274) while sequences can carry 21, so utils/esm.py:52's gather clamps a stop codon to index 19 = 'V'. Two guard branches at constants.py:290,294 are dead (a 20-entry dict has no 'X' key). Separately, scoring/mpnn.py does no AF→MPNN conversion at all (zero hits for `af_to_mpnn|mpnn_to_af`) yet feeds these AF-ordered ints to prxteinmpnn's scorer — a latent vocabulary bug the move to aminx would carry across a repo boundary.

P1a itself is solid: proteinsmc/utils/constants.py:10-37 and proxide/chem/residues.py:622-650 are the same verbatim AlphaFold block, and aminx/utils/aa_convert.py:8-12 ALREADY imports from proxide — the owner is live, not aspirational. §6.6's "4 vocabularies, 3 permutations" census checks out (AF / MPNN / ESM / HHblits; AF↔MPNN, MPNN→ESM, HHblits→AF), and the aminx↔proxide byte-identical duplication is real — but it lives at proxide/io/parsing/mappings.py:25-43 vs aminx/utils/aa_convert.py:19-35, not at chem/residues.py as §4 implies. Note aminx's POTTS_ALPHABET is the same 21-char MPNN string with an identity map (model.py:40-47) — consistent with the corrected potts finding, and correctly not counted as a 5th vocabulary.

P4, the big negative claim, survives where it is load-bearing and fails where it is phrased absolutely. There is NO genetic code table, codon→AA map, translation routine, CAI implementation, or nucleotide substitution model anywhere in proxide, aminx, prolix, xtrax, trex or asr — extraction genuinely has no destination. trex, the flagged risk, has an abstract `cost_matrix`/`n_states` Sankoff (sankoff.py:30,104-132) and zero hits for JC69|HKY|GTR|K80|F81|TN93 (those appear only in asr/src). But "zero DNA/RNA handling" is literally false: proxide deliberately syncs and ships AMBER nucleic force fields (scripts/sync_forcefields.py:52-57 → assets/amber/DNA.bsc1.xml, RNA.OL3.xml, …) and prolix/viewer/src/types.ts:9 tags `"D" | "R"` for DNA/RNA. Both are atom-indexed, so the plan's own qualifier holds — narrow the sentence to "zero codon/translation handling". Two things the plan misses: trex/ground_truth.py:20-52 `mutate()` is the SAME offset-mod-q kernel as proteinsmc's `utils/mutation.py::mutate`, documented in nucleotide terms — an unrecorded collision with the very function §4 routes to `proposals.PointMutation`; and asr already does nucleotide-level work in scripts (q=4 DNA FASTA emission, IQ-TREE alphabet, stop-codon handling), which gives the quarantined codon subpackage a plausible consumer and strengthens §5's recommendation.

P5 must be split. The git-SHA half is confirmed — bathos/git.py:18-40 `capture_git_state` returns hash+branch+dirty, a strict superset of io.py:42's bare `rev-parse HEAD`. The `oed/tracking.py` DELETE is not supported: `rg -i 'checkpoint|resume' bathos/src/bathos` returns three hits, all prose or a CLI message — bathos has no checkpoint system, no equivalent of `save_oed_checkpoint`/`load_oed_checkpoint` (tracking.py:134,177), and nothing resembling the shared-ArrayRecord index cursors (:108,:305,:329), which are data layout rather than provenance. bathos records at process-run granularity; oed/tracking.py records per-BO-iteration inside one process. Those files should travel to asr with the rest of oed/, minus the git shell-out. "5-way git-SHA capture" is also loose: only one library-code site exists outside bathos and xtrax (proteinsmc/io.py:42); the rest are in scripts/.

P3 is confirmed as a single-site claim with a stronger conclusion available than the plan states: `rg --hidden -uu proxide` over the entire repo (tests/, scripts/, test.ipynb included) yields exactly one source hit, scoring/mpnn.py:17 — and proxide is not in pyproject.toml at all, with the import nested inside `if PRXTEINMPNN_AVAILABLE:` (mpnn.py:14). The edge is undeclared and gated on a different package's presence, so "eliminated" costs nothing. It is a genuine runtime dependency though, not a type import: `create_protein_dataset` is called at :84-88 and its outputs closed over at :116-121.

P2's rejection is sound but under-argued. proxide/core/types.py is 140 lines of structure/physics/topology plus a 40-field `SystemParams`; its sequence surface is three lines (:38-40), every alias is built on `ArrayLike = Array | np.ndarray` (:10) which is wrong for a filter_jit contract, and it contains NONE of the population-axis types §3.2 requires (`Population`, `Relaxed`, `Scores`, `LogWeights`, `Ctx`) and no q/alphabet notion. The honest reason is "the destination does not have these types", not "saves ~30 lines".

P6 is confirmed with more severity than stated: the registry at runner.py:54-79 holds six live entries and IS consulted for validation at :176-191, but the executor at :304 is a bare `if == "smc"` with no elif/else, so the other five validate, resolve, leave `final_state = None` (:303), and fall through to the write path having run nothing — a silent no-op, not an error.

HIGHEST-SCRUTINY ITEMS: the two destructive claims are P1b (do not delete `PROTEINMPNN_X_INT` with the alphabet — move it to codon/tables.py and resolve the 20-vs-21 off-by-one as an explicit tested decision) and P5 (do not delete oed/tracking.py's checkpoint and record-index machinery; bathos does not replace it).
groups.assessment:
Mixed. The verifier applied the Potts test correctly and impressively on P1b — it caught that `PROTEINMPNN_X_INT = 21` is named after ProteinMPNN while `AA_CHAR_TO_INT_MAP` is AlphaFold-ordered, and that 21 matches neither convention. I re-read constants.py:113-130, 272-296 and confirm every element of that finding. P2, P3, P4, P6 also hold up under independent reading (proxide/core/types.py:10 `ArrayLike = Array | np.ndarray` with zero population-axis types; `create_protein_dataset` really does exist at proxide/ops/dataset.py:98 and is gated behind `PRXTEINMPNN_AVAILABLE` at mpnn.py:14-17 with proxide absent from pyproject.toml:10-25; aminx/src has literally zero codon/nucleotide hits; runner.py:303-304 confirmed verbatim). The trex `mutate` collision the verifier found is stronger than it stated — trex/ground_truth.py:20-52 and proteinsmc/utils/mutation.py:22-44 share the docstring nearly verbatim, so it is a literal fork, not merely an algorithmic coincidence.

But the verifier fell into the trap in one specific and dangerous way: it confirmed the group's destructive DELETE (P1a) on ordering-equivalence alone. Its entire evidence block for P1a is a character-by-character comparison of two definitions plus a note that aminx already imports proxide's. It never ran a consumer search, never mentions asr, and never asks what breaks. That is exactly the "CONFIRMED delete that was not searched exhaustively" the brief flags as the most dangerous output of the audit. Running that search overturns P1a and P1c both, and surfaces a live cross-repo instance of the very bug the verifier had already diagnosed one repo over.

The second pattern: on P5 the verifier correctly REFUTED the plan's destination (bathos) and then substituted its own destination (asr) with no search at all — replacing an unevidenced claim with another unevidenced claim. asr imports bathos nowhere and has already forked oed/ while deliberately leaving tracking.py behind.

The third pattern is a classic shared-word trap the verifier walked into while explicitly reasoning about shared words: it used aminx's `POTTS_TO_MPNN_ALPHABET_MAP` identity as positive evidence that "potts" contributes no vocabulary. Correct for aminx. But asr's alphabet_reconcile.py defines "Potts order" as gap-FIRST `-ACDEFGHIKLMNPQRSTVWY` — a different alphabet under the same word, in the repo that is the intended destination for oed/.

groups.summary:
Fifteen claims checked against source in proteinsmc, aminx, proxide, prolix, xtrax and asr, plus two live experiments (a JAX/Equinox hashability probe and a minimal ruff TID251 reproduction). Five CONFIRMED, five REFUTED, three NEEDS_QUALIFICATION, two CONFIRMED-with-corrections.

The group's central defect repeats the potts failure mode twice, in the same shape: reasoning from a surface property to a structural conclusion without checking which object the machinery actually touches.

1. §3.1's FATAL-objection evidence is a non-sequitur (S1.3). "Both scorers already close over arrays, therefore both fail `jax.jit(static_argnames=...)`" is false — a closure hashes by identity regardless of what it captures. I ran it: a `@jit` closure over a live `jax.Array` passes as a static argname (`static closure OK`), and so does an undecorated one, which also refutes the "works only because it's `@jit`-decorated" claim (S1.2). What genuinely fails is `Fitness(eqx.Module)` with an array field (`ValueError: Non-hashable static arguments are not supported`, reproduced verbatim). So the remedy — `eqx.filter_jit` — is right, but it is a precondition of the *new* contract, not a fix for a live compilation failure. The plan should stop citing esm.py/mpnn.py as evidence and cite §3.4 instead.

2. §5's "same mechanism aminx already runs" is the inverse of aminx's mechanism (S4.3). I built the proposed rule and ran ruff: banned-api is **global**, so it flags `io.py` (outside the five-module list) and `codon/__init__.py` (the quarantined package importing itself); scoping it needs `per-file-ignores` over the complement, not six lines of TOML. Two silent bypasses survive — `from ..codon import X` (parent-relative) produced `All checks passed!`, as did `importlib.import_module("proteinsmc.codon")`. And `[tool.ruff] exclude` already drops `tests`, where 15 codon-touching files live. aminx bans other subsystems' modules with one exemption; proteinsmc would ban its own subpackage and exempt everything but five files.

Three further findings that change work estimates rather than verdicts:
- **`_run_prsmc_chunk`'s filter_jit conversion is not mechanical** (S2.3, high blast radius). `config_to_jax` (sampler_base.py:340-344) turns every int config field into a jnp array, and `n_exchange_attempts` is used as a *shape* at parallel_replica.py:95-100 and 350-355. Today that is a hard unhashable-static error; under filter_jit it becomes a silent ConcretizationTypeError unless those four params are explicitly re-staticised.
- **The five-line CI grep cannot catch the cycle the plan creates** (S2.2, high). Entry-point registration yields aminx -> proteinsmc -> `entry_points()` -> aminx at runtime with no `aminx` token in proteinsmc's source. Needs lazy resolution plus a clean-venv `sys.modules` assertion.
- **Counts are wrong in both §3.2 and §5.** Point-form kernels are 4 of 6 registered, not "3 of 8" (S3.1) — and *every* current kernel consumes the point form, so batched-by-default changes 100% of the kernel surface. The "13-file" codon path enumerates 11 and omits ~7, the worst being `models/smc.py:26,28`'s nucleotide-named `PopulationSequences`, imported straight into `sampling/particle_systems/smc.py:23,118` — inside the core the quarantine exists to protect (S4.1). There is also a fifth incompatible fitness contract Phase 0 misses, at `initialization_factory.py:350-368` (S3.3).

Two of the plan's own internal contradictions surfaced: §4's "`needs_translation` is the mechanism by which codons leak" is refuted by its own §5 point 1, which correctly names `TranslateFuncSignature` (S4.2); and §4 rejects adopting `key_management.py` because it would change the PRNG stream, while §3.2's batched-fitness adoption changes it too (S2.3).

Nothing in this group is destructive, and no DELETE claim fell in it. The §5 "keep it as `proteinsmc/codon/`" recommendation survives — the negative search backing it is genuinely clean (0 codon/nucleotide hits in .py/.rs across proxide, aminx, prolix, xtrax; only vendored OpenMM nucleic-acid force-field XML in proxide's assets). It is the *enforcement mechanism*, not the placement decision, that does not hold up.
groups.assessment:
Partially. The verifier applied the potts test well on two claims — S4.2 (it read `needs_translation`'s body and correctly separated the *word* "translation" from the injected `TranslateFuncSignature` callable that actually carries the codon dependency) and S1.3/S1.4 (it refused to infer unhashability from "closes over arrays" and ran a real experiment on the exact proposed shape). Those are model applications.

But it applied the test only *inside* proteinsmc, and never turned it on the plan's foundational premise. Plan §1 line 9 says "aminx structurally *cannot* host that — `aminx/pyproject.toml:143-169` enforces ADR 260605 ... i.e. aminx has already ruled by lint that a non-StageSet iterative sampler cannot live in its main body." That is the potts error verbatim: a lint wall read as a domain exclusion. The verifier read that exact TOML block twice (in S2.1 and S4.3) and never asked what it actually bans, nor whether aminx already hosts an iterative sampler. It does: `aminx/src/aminx/potts/sampling.py` is 618 LOC of "Single-site Gibbs updates and parallel tempering." Every downstream verdict in this group (S2.1, S2.2, S4.3) sits on top of an unchallenged premise that is false.

Second systematic gap: it never verified a single *destination*. The ground rules say a move claim asserts two things; the verifier checked only "should it leave." It never ran `rg esm` against aminx (0 hits — aminx has zero ESM), and it never searched `asr` on any claim, despite asr vendoring proteinsmc, importing it in 12 files, and being named in the ground rules as mandatory search scope. Its S4.4 CONFIRMED negative covers four repos and omits the one that matters.

Third: its two live experiments were good practice but one was mis-set-up and reported a false negative (S4.3's parent-relative bypass), and the other used a synthetic `jnp.ones` closure standing in for scorers it never actually tried to construct — one of which cannot be constructed in this environment at all.
